root.note: Taíno was spoken in the Caribbean. Wiktionary has Portuguese borrowing the word through Spanish.

history: Batata is one of the first American words to reach Europe. The Taíno people of the Caribbean called the sweet potato batata, and Spanish sailors brought plant and word back after 1492. Portuguese took the word from Spanish. Then a second plant arrived from the Andes, the potato, called papa in Quechua. Spanish mixed the two names into patata, and English took potato from that. Portuguese kept the Taíno word for both and adds a label to the original: batata-doce, ‘sweet potato’. Today batatas are on every Portuguese table, as batatas fritas, ‘chips’, or batatas a murro, small potatoes roasted in their skins and given a ‘punch’ to crack them open.
historyEinfach: Batata means ‘potato’. The word comes from Taíno, a language of the Caribbean. There, batata was the sweet potato. Spanish sailors brought the word to Europe. Portuguese says batata-doce for the sweet potato. English potato comes from the same word.

cognates.note: a mix of batata and Quechua papa

elsewhere.text: English potato is the Caribbean word, passed on by Spanish.
The Andean name of the potato. Portuguese never took it.
